clue.text: Time to make a choice with skill where guests will sit at dinner

definitions.text: where guests will sit at dinner

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to opt is to make a choice
skilled, capable; read as 'with skill' = able

explanation.surface: A host deciding cleverly on the seating plan for a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the skill to the choice, and the skill gives a word meaning capable.
explanation.definitionFit: The top table is the head table at a banquet or wedding, reserved for the hosts and principal guests.

clue.text: Drink a lot of Best and start on Export

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
the start of a word is its opening letter, which is the one kept

blocks.note: the tops is informal for the very best
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A drinker downing plenty of Best bitter and then starting on the Export lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Best and Export look like beer brands, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is an old word for drinking alcohol heavily and habitually; a toper is a drunkard.

clue.text: I conceal dope, his undoing?

indicators.note: undoing means unpicking and taking apart, so the letters before it are reassembled differently

blocks.note: all fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisoner boasting that the drug they have slipped in will bring the victim down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a cup that hides a drug which proves the drinker's undoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is a gift or post that looks attractive but ruins the person who accepts it.

clue.text: Enquire about strange rites in star-shaped figure

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order
about means around, so one piece goes round the outside of the other

blocks.note: to ask is to enquire
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone investigating odd ceremonies conducted within a pentagram.
explanation.walkthrough: AS-K goes round the rearranged rites. 'star-shaped figure' sounds occult but is the printed mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The asterisk is the typographic symbol shaped like a little star, its name coming from the Greek for star.

clue.text: S-sheep, not black, a provider of wool

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter standing for the colour is taken away

blocks.note: the stutter is copied onto a young sheep, repeating its first letter
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stammering shepherd naming a sheep that is not black but still gives wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer in 'S-sheep' is not to be read literally: it tells you to stutter the word for a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American camelid kept for its soft fleece, which is spun into wool.

clue.text: Intensely cold drink

blocks.note: first meaning: biting, piercing cold
second meaning: a British style of hoppy draught beer

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an iced drink, but the two parts are separate meanings; bitter is a British pub beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes weather that stings with cold, and the noun is a kind of ale served in British pubs.

clue.text: Where this girl must end up?

definitions.text: Where this girl must end up?

blocks.clueFragment: Where this girl must end up?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about some young woman's fate or destination
setter's reading: the girl is this very answer, whose name must finish up written into the squares of the puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a woman's name that also splits as a phrase saying where a solved answer goes: into the crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the name describes the position of every completed answer, entered among the puzzle's squares.

clue.text: A boast even at a bet? It's nothing but a story

definitions.text: A boast even at a bet? It's nothing but a story

blocks.clueFragment: A boast even at a bet?
blocks.note: surface reading: a bragging claim made as a wager
setter's reading: the answer is a work of fiction, a famous comic novel

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic novel about a Thames boating holiday; the question mark flags the playful lead-in.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a well-known humorous English novel, so it is indeed a story.

clue.text: Dance to sound of genuine kind of old recorder

indicators.note: sound of means the word is heard rather than seen, so its spoken form is spelt another way

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish country dance
taken as written
a word meaning genuine, said out loud

explanation.surface: Dancing to the authentic sound of an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' suggests the woodwind instrument, but it is a tape machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Reel-to-reel tape recorders, with open spools, preceded cassettes and are now largely obsolete.

clue.text: Strike-breaker British want to get on

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
want in the sense of shortage, a lack
in cricket the on side of the field is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A British worker eager to carry on working during a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' looks like a verb of desire; it is the noun meaning shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackleg is the derogatory British term for a worker who carries on working during a strike, a scab.

clue.text: Pawn isn't taking bishop — completely messy game

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
all, as in 'all wet', means completely

explanation.surface: A chess complaint: a pawn declining to capture a bishop makes the whole game a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' sounds like a chess capture; here it only means the bishop is added on next.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat game in which players shoot each other with pellets that burst into splashes of paint.

clue.text: Note, rambling rose is a prickly shrub

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters stray out of their order

blocks.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
the four letters of the flower, rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener observing that a rambling rose has turned into a thorny bush.
explanation.walkthrough: A rambling rose is a real climbing rose, which is why 'rambling' hides so well as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny evergreen shrub with yellow flowers, common on heaths; another name for it is furze.

clue.text: Petty officer leading men is deserving of pity

blocks.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A naval officer in charge of the men cuts a pitiable figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' just places the officer first.
explanation.definitionFit: We say 'poor thing' of someone who arouses sympathy, so the adjective carries the sense of pitiable.

clue.text: Perhaps Scott of the Arctic? That's wrong

indicators.note: the phrase says something is in error, so the preceding letters are set right by rearranging them

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A pedant pointing out that Captain Scott explored the Antarctic, not the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is right that Scott of the Antarctic is wrongly placed; the Scott meant is Giles Gilbert Scott, who designed Liverpool Cathedral and the red telephone box.
explanation.definitionFit: Several famous Scotts, notably Giles Gilbert Scott and George Gilbert Scott, were designers of buildings, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: I'll hear duo playing — one gives sound more volume

indicators.note: playing suggests performing freely, so the letters before it are arranged in a new way

blocks.note: all ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A concert-goer resolving to hear two musicians perform, through an amplifier.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudhailer is a hand-held megaphone that amplifies the voice so it carries further.

clue.text: Provide with too much more than drink to work steadily

blocks.note: over means more than, as in over forty
to sup is to drink in sips
to ply a trade is to work at it steadily

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks more than they should, supposedly to keep working.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversupply is to furnish more of something than is wanted, a glut.

clue.text: What may give damage in a china shop?

definitions.text: What may give damage in a china shop?

blocks.clueFragment: What may give damage in a china shop?
blocks.note: surface reading: the proverbial bull that smashes crockery
setter's reading: damage is informal for the cost, as in 'what's the damage?', shown on a label in any shop

explanation.walkthrough: The bull in a china shop is the false path; 'what's the damage?' is everyday British slang asking how much something costs.
explanation.definitionFit: The label attached to goods shows how much they cost, which is the bill or damage.

clue.text: Good appreciation of music equipment

blocks.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
to have an ear for music is to appreciate it

explanation.surface: A musician with a good ear and the right instruments and amplifiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is the general word for kit or apparatus, such as climbing gear or camera gear.

clue.text: What new driller for oil has got prosperous?

definitions.text: What new driller for oil has got

blocks.clueFragment: What new driller for oil has got
blocks.note: first meaning, read as a phrase: a borehole still to be sunk, a job ahead
second meaning: comfortably off

explanation.walkthrough: Split into words, the answer says a new oilman has a bore yet to sink; joined up it means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do is an idiom for wealthy, and an oil driller striking it rich makes the surface apt too.

clue.text: Where one might repair cutter for weed

blocks.note: first meaning: a cutter is a small boat, mended in a dry harbour basin
second meaning: a broad-leaved weed of fields and verges

explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a lawnmower or blade for clearing weeds; it is a sailing boat. The weed is the plant whose leaves are rubbed on nettle stings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry dock is where ships are repaired, and the dock is a common weed with large leaves.

clue.text: One behind another unique dossier

blocks.note: single means one and only, unique
a dossier is a file of documents on a person or topic

explanation.surface: A secret dossier, one of a kind, kept on someone who is following another.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in single file means moving in a line, each person directly behind the one in front.

clue.text: Language that's grand and universal in general character

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the pair goes within the longer word

blocks.note: G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
the tone of a place or event is its general character

explanation.surface: Praise for a language that is noble and widely shared in its overall nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand and universal' read as praise, but they are two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue is an old and literary word for a language, as in mother tongue.

clue.text: Down below a bat flutters

indicators.note: fluttering things flap about irregularly, so the letters before it are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Feathers drifting beneath a bat as it flits about in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' reads as soft feathers in the surface; it is the adjective for feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at a low ebb, like a tide that has gone out, is to be dejected or depressed, as is feeling down.

clue.text: Steep sided hill having not entirely spread

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a spread for bread

explanation.surface: A hill whose slopes have not fully spread out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' reads as a verb in the surface; it is the noun for what goes on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A butte is an isolated flat-topped hill with steep sides, typical of the American West.

clue.text: Word used in Anglo-American for soil

indicators.note: a word used in a phrase is contained within it, so the letters are found inside the following words

blocks.note: the end of Anglo running into the start of American

explanation.surface: A question of transatlantic vocabulary: what Britons and Americans each call dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Loam is a fertile soil of clay, sand and humus, prized by gardeners.

clue.text: Sort of radial with a single diagonal cut

indicators.note: a single slanting stroke added under the loop of one capital turns it into a different capital letter

blocks.note: a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: A description of a radial with one slanting incision in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw one diagonal stroke down from the bowl of a capital P and it becomes R. A radial is a radial-ply tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a car tyre whose cord plies run at right angles to the tread, so the noun stands for the whole wheel covering.

clue.text: Prone to be telling fibs

blocks.note: first meaning
second meaning: not telling the truth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone to' looks like 'inclined to'; here prone stands alone, meaning stretched out flat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both reclining horizontally and saying things that are untrue.

clue.text: Science that's looking up?

blocks.note: surface reading: a branch of science whose prospects are improving
setter's reading: literally gazing upward at the sky and the stars

explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking up' is the idiom for improving; the question mark invites the literal sense of staring at the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy is the scientific study of stars, planets and other celestial bodies, done by observing the sky above.

clue.text: Canvas trimmer producing a roll of hemp

blocks.note: first meaning: a sailor who takes in sail, shortening the canvas in a strong wind
second meaning: a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas trimmer' suggests a sailmaker's or artist's cutter; trimming canvas is reducing sail, done by reefing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who reefs sails is a reefer, and reefer is also slang for a joint, cannabis being a form of hemp.

clue.text: Regularly trapped in Dieppe, our steerer is one for whom transportation is punishing

definitions.text: one for whom transportation is punishing

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter caught inside the following words is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A Channel ferry from Dieppe, its helmsman finding the crossing a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Transportation was the old legal penalty of shipping convicts overseas, so here it is a punishment rather than travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A deportee is someone expelled from a country, for whom being sent away is the penalty itself.
